title: BLOW UP your ARMS with these 3 GIANT sets (Biceps/Triceps/Forearms)
summary: He gives three plug-in arm giant sets (overall arms, triceps-focused, biceps-focused) so lifters can add arm isolation without sacrificing compounds. He explains the ordering logic: freshest priority lift first, respect the intensity pyramid, use abs or forearm work as active rest, and place them on upper days away from overlapping sessions.
claims: A big torso with skinny arms gives a 'spider physique'; you must isolate the arms
Giant sets let you add arm isolation without sacrificing compounds, and arms are small muscles so the added fatigue won't sabotage the program
His programs are puzzle pieces; the aim is to teach you to program for yourself
Each arm giant set is 3 exercises done for 3-4 rounds, and even within a giant set you can bias the focus toward one muscle
Overall-arm giant set for those not advanced enough for an arm day: any curl 6-12, then triceps pushdowns (lateral head) or French press (long head) 8-12, then wrist or finger curls 10-15
If new to arm isolation, start with just the curl and triceps pair and add the forearm work later when you recover better
Swap exercises only for ones hitting the same muscles; changing the pattern creates a different giant set with a different result
Put the overall-arm giant set into an upper day where you don't train arms directly
Triceps giant set: close-grip bench 6-10, then skull crushers or French press 8-12, then leg raises or dragon flags AMRAP
Proper skull crushers mostly train the triceps long head
The ab exercise in the triceps giant set is active rest so you are fresher for the close-grip bench next round
The first movement of a giant set is the one you want freshest: a compound or the lift you prioritize
Respect the intensity pyramid: never put a heavy compound like a block pull after lateral raises in a giant set
The filler slot can be abs, calves, neck or rear delts; you can never train abs or calves too much
Biceps giant set: chin-ups AMRAP (or weighted 3-5), then reverse curls 6-12, then Arnold curls or close-grip preacher curls 6-10
Reverse curls sit between chin-ups and curls so the biceps aren't pre-fatigued right before curling and the forearms get trained while grip isn't the limiter
If chin-up performance drops in the biceps giant set, remove one of the curls
Simpler option: chin-ups superset with hammer or pinwheel curls; less volume and quality tonnage but workable
Place these giant sets on an upper day away from other sessions hitting the same muscles; don't add the triceps set on bench day unless close-grip bench is your bench variation
exercises: 6-12 reps, opener of the overall-arm giant set
6-10 reps, first in triceps giant set
hits biceps and forearms in one movement
